ordered_diagnoses: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma of the Iris

facts.raw_span: A man in his late 60s presented for evaluation of a right iris lesion
Visual acuity was 20/25 OU
The eye was pseudophakic
10 × 9 × 3.5-mm, well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan, peripheral iris nodule between the 3- and 6-o'clock positions
episcleral sentinel vessels and anterior chamber angle involvement
no visible iris seeding or aqueous cells
Ultrasonographic biomicroscopy: Showed ciliary body involvement
Fine-needle aspiration biopsy results: Showed monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes
Few CD3+, reactive T lymphocytes were present
Systemic evaluation: Showed no other involvement
Staging: T2N0M0
Image A: Well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan iris lesion

concepts.why: The presence of a well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan iris nodule and the biopsy results showing a monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes support the diagnosis of primary iris lymphoma.

The presence of a well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan iris nodule and the biopsy results showing a monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes, along with the presence of few CD3+, reactive T lymphocytes, support the diagnosis of iris marginal zone lymphoma.

concepts.preferred_label: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma of the Iris
concepts.why: The presence of a well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan iris nodule and the biopsy results showing a monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes, along with the staging results, support the diagnosis of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of the iris.

The presence of a well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan iris nodule and the systemic evaluation showing no other involvement support the diagnosis of iris metastasis, although the primary site is unknown.

The presence of episcleral sentinel vessels and anterior chamber angle involvement, along with the absence of visible iris seeding or aqueous cells, support the diagnosis of iris inflammation, although the underlying cause is unknown.
The presence of a well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan iris nodule supports the diagnosis of iris melanoma, although the biopsy results do not support this diagnosis.
It explains the ciliary body involvement shown on ultrasonographic biomicroscopy.

rationales.F04: The presence of a well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan iris nodule is highly suggestive of a lymphoma.
rationales.F05: The presence of episcleral sentinel vessels and anterior chamber angle involvement is highly suggestive of a lymphoma.
rationales.F07: The ciliary body involvement seen on ultrasonographic biomicroscopy is highly suggestive of a lymphoma.
rationales.F08: The presence of a monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes on fine-needle aspiration biopsy is highly suggestive of a lymphoma.
rationales.F11: The staging of T2N0M0 suggests a localized disease, which is consistent with a primary iris lymphoma.
